title: r/longevity on Reddit: Rapamycin + acarbose "longest lived males we ever got" in the ITP studies; fisetin did not show benefit or senolytic activity | Dr. Rich Miller on Live Longer World
abstract:
The 3 labs did not find lifespan extension from fisetin and even moreso, did not find that fisetin reduced senescent cells. ... They saw no senolytic activity from fisetin (in mice), so it sounds like yes that is correct.
The 3 labs did not find lifespan extension from fisetin and even moreso, did not find that fisetin reduced senescent cells. ... They saw no senolytic activity from fisetin (in mice), so it sounds like yes that is correct.
The senolytic concept is not a strong one. I’m not an advocate for most of Blagosklonny’s online behavior but he knows his shit on this one. Senescent cells are hard to target, not strictly speaking zombie cells, and of questionable value from a therapeutic perspective at this point. Even Kirkland says it probably won’t work in people. ... The fisetin result is disappointing.
In the case that fisetin simply lacks this functionality I fear we'll need to wait years for a proper test re senolysis and lifespan. Wish they had tried dasatinib instead. ... It sounds like the mice in the ITP trial didn't have any senescent cells to begin with (about 55:00). Not sure how this is possible. Also not sure how the study can disprove an effect against inflammation and senolytic activity when these measures weren't tested for.
Reasons to hope to see the age of 100 and beyond: Biomedical rejuvenation through damage repair, manipulation of metabolism, beyond the mere results of exercise, caloric restriction, and fasting. Stem cell therapies, anti-cancer viruses, gene therapy, senolytics, and whatever is coming next...
